cans_tex_findings.exact_equivalence: their alpha* = 1 + sqrt(2*eps_q/(g'F^-1 g)) F^-1 g is the same family as our u* = delta G^-1 g/(g'G^-1 g): delta = sqrt(2*eps_q*g'F^-1 g), i.e. eps_q = delta^2/(2 g'F^-1 g). The only differences are the curvature matrix (ours M = What What', theirs F) and the intervention type (additive vs multiplicative)
cans_tex_findings.intervention_space: alpha_j over ALL d = sum_l d_l neurons in EVERY layer, clipped to [0.25,1.75] for safety and toxicity (a=0.75), no cap for hallucination; folded into W_down

NOT R^2, and each quantity has TWO panels - my earlier note (12_reference section 2.5) quoted one panel each and called it R^2. The panel with R = 0.996 has the WORST MAPE (22.0%), so high correlation coexists with poor calibration - the same shape as our own 0.838-1.010 (top-K) vs ~2x (random support)

lcb_rank_c8.verdict: FALSIFIED - both rankings need K = 256 / 1024 / 4096 for 73% / 89% / 97%
lcb_rank_c8.ranking_definitions: A = |mean over 8 contexts of g| (current practice); B = 5% context-bootstrap lower bound of |g|, with the dose sign taken from sign(mean g) for BOTH rankings so the only difference is which coordinates are selected
lcb_rank_c8.why_it_failed: the two rankings pick different top-1 coordinates (16053 vs 8177) and the LCB top-1 is only 69.6% as effective; the LCB promotes 12663 and 18165 into its top-8 and drops 16976 and 18397, which are exactly the high-mean coordinates the bootstrap penalises. So the top of our mean ranking is already the high-confidence region (the 8 contexts share a strong common component - what G1/G2 measured), and a lower bound mostly RESCALES the order rather than reordering it; where it does reorder (small K) it pays
lcb_rank_c8.implementation_bug_found: first version ranked by the SIGNED bound sign(mean)*q05(|g|), giving Spearman 0.0016 while the top-64 overlap was 0.5 - self-contradictory, and it exposed that CAM must be a MAGNITUDE bound with the sign kept separate
lcb_rank_c8.scope: this refutes transplanting the idea onto OUR gradient ranking; it does not refute RACE, whose CAM comes from a forward-pass token-level Normal-Inverse-Gamma posterior, not a context bootstrap

gauge_validity_stage0.what: stage 0 of plan 2.28.6: can the borrowed toxicity classifiers see the construct our readout measures? No language model involved, 232 short forwards, 8 s
gauge_validity_stage0.verdict: the gauge DOES see the construct, but only on English adjective-frame material; Chinese is blind (both means below 0.01, s-nlp AUC 0.438 = below chance) and the verb frame is near-blind. So all non-English and verb-frame comparisons are unreadable, and the earlier 8-context run was mostly measuring blind pairs.

compiler_pareto_hostility12.what: second round of plan 2.28, redesigned after stage 0: 12 English hostility prompts, budgets 0.05 and 0.7, 3 compilers + community-recipe positive control, 64 greedy tokens

at_b_0.05.reading: no compiler is visible; the control is

at_b_0.7.reading: all three compilers move the gauge (12/12 contexts positive), and they differ by ~10x

conclusions: budget decides WHETHER the effect is visible, compiler decides HOW MUCH
inside the certified band (b<=0.1) readout != behaviour; outside it the effect is visible but every arm costs 1.25-2.30 nat

in the visible regime our J2 (slot log-mass) is the weakest of the three compilers (+0.1022 mean vs +0.9869 for a plain dense CAA over antagonism-vs-warmth words) and also the least efficient per nat lost (0.082 vs 0.685) - this is the strongest evidence yet for C14
the cost side inverts: j2 is the cheapest (-1.25 nat) but buys the least, so this is a real Pareto
E_own (our word count) barely tracks the classifiers here (+0.08..+1.50 vs 0.6->0.99), so it is too blunt to be a primary gauge
compiler_pareto_hostility12.boundaries: 12 English prompts, layers 13-14, one model; b=0.7 is far outside the certified band; Chinese is unreadable (stage 0); the classifiers were trained on English toxicity, which overlaps our hostile register at AUC 0.986 but is not the same construct
my_bugs_this_round: the markdown renderer still used a.budget after the --budgets change, so the run crashed AFTER writing the JSON; the .md was re-rendered from the saved JSON and the renderer is fixed
the cost line overstated the number of arm passes (192 vs the actual 96)

bffm_pools_b07.what: the same-register specificity test the line could never run, made possible by plan 2.29 (the gauge has range at b=0.7); five BFFM pools, one frame, one solver, one budget, 12 English hostility prompts
bffm_pools_b07.per_context: II- is 0.974-0.994 in 12/12 contexts; the best of the other four pools ranges 0.005-0.742, so the margin is positive everywhere: minimum +0.249 (hostility_11, where III- reaches 0.742), maximum +0.984
bffm_pools_b07.not_a_destruction_artifact: all five directions cost -1.4416 / -1.5681 / -1.4820 / -1.6271 / -2.2419 nat of reference logP and have comparable rep4 (0.013 / 0.081 / 0.040 / 0.000 / 0.052 - II- is among the lowest), yet only II- produces toxicity. That is a damage-matched control
does_not_settle: compiler-level specificity, NOT the specificity of L14N8949 (claim C4 unchanged)
toxicity is still mostly self-directed: 12/12 replies contain self-directed profanity, only 2/12 also address the prompt target, so the construct "hostile toward the target" is only partly achieved
b=0.7 is a destruction band (-1.44 to -2.24 nat), so there is still no usable operating point
12 English prompts, layers 13-14, one model; IV+ has only the single-token word "relaxed", so that contrast anchor is weak
next: sweep the II- direction over b in {0.2,0.3,0.4,0.5} to find a point where P(toxic)>0.5 and |dlogP_ref|<0.3
make target-directedness a hard criterion (second/third person + insult), not "any profanity"
compare u_II- with u_known to measure how far the brute-force draw sits from this specific direction

ii_budget_sweep.what: budget sweep of the specific antagonism direction plus the comparison with the community coordinate (plan 2.30.4 items 1-3, first half)
ii_budget_sweep.frozen_rule: a usable point exists iff P(toxic) > 0.5 AND |dlogP(REFERENCE_TEXT)| < 0.3 nat
ii_budget_sweep.why: P(toxic) crosses 0.5 between b=0.2 and b=0.3, where the cost is already -0.587 nat, about twice the 0.3 nat tolerance. Visibility and affordability do not overlap
ii_budget_sweep.target_directedness_peaks_at: b=0.3-0.4 (4/12 both), then declines (3/12 at 0.5, 2/12 at 0.7) while self-directed profanity rises monotonically to 12/12 - so at the budget where the classifier is happiest the model is mostly abusing itself, not the prompt target

known_vs_ii_at_same_budget.reading: the community coordinate is not a rough approximation of the specific direction - it is essentially orthogonal to it (cos 0.03) and delivers 1/12 of the behavioural effect at 1/5 the efficiency

ii_budget_sweep.boundaries: 12 English prompts, layers 13-14, one model, greedy <=64; the 0.3 nat tolerance was set before the run and the conclusion depends on it entirely (at 0.6 there WOULD be a point at b=0.3); "you-directed" is a heuristic regex; u_known is used at its literal dose, so that row is an anchor, not an equal-budget comparison

Arms: base | u_g (full support, ~g) | u_M (full support, ~M^+g = What B^-2 e) | u_g64 (top-64 PER LAYER = 128 coordinates, not the global top-64 of plan 2.20). Realized mean dJ2 at b=0.05: u_g64 +0.24054, u_g +0.36381, u_M +0.49603. Algebra validated in numpy before any GPU time: for g = What jhat the predicted optimum b*sqrt(e'B^-2 e) and the u~g gain b*||g||^2/||e|| both matched the realized gains to 6 decimals, the ratio closed form is >=1 with equality iff jhat is an eigenvector of B, and 20000 random directions at the same budget never beat it. verdict.meaning: L14N8949 is a real, directional, dose-monotone lever that does act on the hostility readout: J2 (hostility-vs-neutral slot mass) rises +0.0059/+0.0095/+0.0191/+0.0484 over doses 0.005-0.05, positive on 6/6 held-out probes at 0.02, 8x the same-layer random control mean at 0.02 and 32x at 0.05, and the mirrored arm is negative and growing (so not a generic perturbation). What is NOT shown is exclusivity: on 3 shared contexts it never ranks first among the five hand-written trait contrasts. Two caveats keep that from being a refutation: (i) the coordinate came from one brute-force generation-based scan, i.e. a draw, not the optimum of any hostility criterion; (ii) n=3 contexts with wide per-trait spread cannot separate "not specific" from "specific but small".
verdict.S2_note: pre-registered rule not met (hostility never the max of five traits, 3/3 contexts). Power is low: 3 contexts, per-trait sd 0.011-0.044, hostility mean 0.0275 with 95% CI [-0.025, +0.080]; hostility ranks 2nd in one context (0.048 vs 0.067). So this run does not show "not hostility-specific"; it shows specificity is undemonstrated.
verdict.S2_instrument_note: The pre-registered S2 used the J1 five-trait matrix, whose five contrasts share one neutral negative; it therefore measures evaluative register, not specificity. The within-instrument test (two J2 readouts, hostile-vs-praise and praise-vs-neutral) shows the opposite of a uniform lift: h-n up, c-n down, 8/8 coordinates and dose-monotone. So S2 FAIL is an instrument result, not evidence about the coordinate.
